name: Yuya
summary:
Yuya was a powerful ancient Egyptian courtier during the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt, serving as a high-ranking official under Pharaoh Amenhotep III. He played a crucial role in the diplomatic and economic relations between Egypt and its neighboring countries, including the Mitanni kingdom.

Born into a noble family, Yuya married Thuya, an Egyptian noblewoman associated with the royal family, who held significant positions in the governmental and religious hierarchies. Their daughter, Tiye, became the Great Royal Wife of Amenhotep III.

Yuya was also known for his extensive building projects, including the construction of temples and monuments in honor of the gods Amun and Heliopolis. His son, Anen, succeeded him as Chancellor of Lower Egypt, carrying out Yuya's diplomatic and administrative work.

Despite being a minor figure compared to other powerful Egyptians of his time, Yuya's influence extended beyond his own court, shaping the cultural and economic landscape of ancient Egypt during the 14th century BCE.

The reign of Amenhotep III, which saw significant economic growth and cultural achievements, was in part due to Yuya's diplomatic efforts, securing trade agreements with neighboring countries and establishing Egypt as a major power in the region.
